title: Five Architectures, One Shared Space Cross-Model Representational Alignment Without Weight Merging
abstract: arXiv:2610.33495v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Combining language models is usually done by averaging weights, which works only when the models share a common starting point. We ask whether five frozen, independently trained models with different internal designs (four transformers from four organizations and one state-space model) can be related through their activations alone, with no weight merging. Using permutation tests, an independent replication probe set, depth sweeps, pooling ablations and confound checks, we find statistically robust correspondence between how the five models organize the same text. It is strongest at each model's final layer and weaker for the state-space model, whose weakest pairing is still 35-43 times chance. We use this to build a shared space with Generalized Procrustes Analysis, in which no model is a fixed reference. translated_title: 五种架构，一个共享空间：无需权重合并的跨模型表征对齐

tldr: 研究发现五个独立训练、架构各异的语言模型（四个Transformer和一个状态空间模型）无需权重合并，仅通过激活值分析和广义Procrustes分析即可构建共享表征空间，最后一层的留出检索准确率高达0.91至0.93。
en_tdlr: Five independently trained language models with different architectures (four Transformers and one state-space model) can be aligned into a shared representational space through activation analysis and Generalized Procrustes Analysis alone—without weight merging—achieving 0.91 to 0.93 held-out retrieval accuracy at the final layer.
